extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international and Cold War affairs
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and summarizing international political, economic and diplomatic developments related to the Soviet Union, Eastern Europe, China and Western responses during the early Cold War period. Includes speech excerpts, policy statements, trial reports and related news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on atomic energy (peaceful use vs. weapons)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the heads of the imperialists atomic energy is a means for the production of lethal weapons, a means of intimidation, an instrument of blackmail and coercion. But in the hands of the Soviet people it can be and must be an instrument of technical ... progress on a scale never witnessed before, an instrument for the further rapid development of the productive forces of our country."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames atomic energy as either a weapon of imperialist coercion or a peaceful instrument of progress; implies policy: pursue peaceful applications, oppose military/foreign-expansion uses. (Surrounding text: Soviet Government calls for outlawing the atomic weapon and for international control.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for unconditional outlawing and international control of the atomic weapon
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Soviet Government ... proposes the condemnation of the preparations being conducted in certain countries ... for a new war, the unconditional outlawing of the atomic weapon; and the establishment of suitable international control."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes concrete diplomatic/legal remedies: condemn preparations for war, legally outlaw atomic arms unconditionally, and create international control mechanisms. Acknowledges political obstacles: "It is possible that the instigators of war will disrupt this proposal."

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for a correct solution of the German question
rubrics_metrics.description: "European and consequently international peace cannot be insured without the correct solution of the German question. The German question cannot be solved unless German democracy takes into its own hands the fate of its country, if it does not deprive the Ruhr magnates of their economic and political basis, unless it carries out in the country radical democratic changes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a political standard/requirement for resolving postwar German issues: German democratic forces must assume control, break the economic/political power of industrial magnates (Ruhr magnates), and implement radical democratic reforms. Uses the establishment of the German Democratic Republic as evidence that prerequisites are forming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators used to claim socialist economic superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Speech asserts measurable economic indicators demonstrating socialism's superiority: increases in "gross industrial output," output exceeding prewar levels, productivity gains (example: "the productivity of labor in industry was 14 per cent higher than last year"), large deliveries of tractors/harvesting machines to agriculture, increases in livestock and agricultural deliveries, housing built or rebuilt ("living space of over 61,000,000 square meters"), and comparisons of unemployment and trade declines in capitalist countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses specific economic statistics and comparisons (percent increases, production volumes, machinery distributions, housing figures, unemployment counts) as criteria to evaluate and argue for the superiority/stability of the socialist economic system versus capitalist economies. Examples and numeric claims are provided as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting political signals from official displays (portraits as clues)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The exhibition of the portraits is a traditional clue to shifts in the Politburo ... The absence of Kaganovich's portrait indicated he had been dropped" (as reported by AP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats public/state ceremonial displays (who is pictured, who is omitted) as an interpretive metric for detecting personnel or power shifts within a ruling body. Example: omission of a portrait used as evidence to infer a change in standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose and punishment of espionage/diversion as proof of anti-imperialist intrigues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting asserts that trials such as the Budapest trial of Rajk and his accomplices "showed that the warmongers and their Yugoslav lackeys stop at nothing" and that the exposure "struck a heavy blow against the intrigues of the imperialists. ... the mask has been torn off, the perfidious plans have been exposed, the criminals caught at the scene of the crime."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats public trials and exposures of spy/diversionist networks as a criterion/evidence for demonstrating foreign interference and justifying domestic/foreign policy responses; uses the trial outcome as a political signal and proof of external hostile activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peace-strengthening measures and diplomatic proposals as criteria for sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Text repeatedly advances that genuine peace policy requires concrete measures: condemning warmongering preparations, forming pacts among major powers ("the five great powers ... conclude a pact ... for the strengthening of peace"), and extending international controls and condemnations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the sincerity and effectiveness of peace-oriented actors by whether they propose and pursue concrete collective measures (pacts, condemnations, international controls) rather than rhetoric; acknowledges such proposals may be obstructed by 'instigators of war.'
